explainedBy: The Pinto is labouring up the hill to the farm: a sealed car whose engine is failing.

storyboard.claim: The car is struggling up the unpaved hill.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sealed Pinto box on a rising dirt hill, Donna at the wheel and Tad beside her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the car passage; the sealed car is the object the next beats follow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the car as the sealed box that will later become an oven.

explainedBy: The speedometer needle falls from 40 to 30 as the engine bucks and dies.

storyboard.claim: The car is losing power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same car stage; Donna afraid, Tad worried beside her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same car; the speed falls.
storyboard.addedInformation: The speed drop is the first measurable sign of the failure.

explainedBy: The warning light on the dash flickers as the exhaust backfires.

storyboard.claim: The dashboard warning light flickers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same car; Donna glancing worried, the car unchanged around her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same car; a second warning sign.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dash light is the second warning, named on screen.

explainedBy: The car rolls into the driveway on its last momentum, and the engine dies.

storyboard.claim: The engine dies and the car stops.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same car stopped in the driveway; both faces afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same car, now stopped.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stop is the result of the failing sequence.

explainedBy: The engine is silent: the car is dead and they are stuck.

storyboard.claim: Total silence after the engine dies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The stopped car; Donna blank, Tad sad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stopped car, the silence settles in.
storyboard.addedInformation: The silence is the stillness of the dead car.

explainedBy: The breakdown happens in the worst place they could be.

storyboard.claim: The breakdown is in the worst possible place.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The stopped car on the empty farm road; Donna neutral, Tad sad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stopped car, now the place is named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the location as the problem.

explainedBy: We trust a car to move when we turn the key; the hand reaches for it.

storyboard.claim: We trust technology to start when we turn the key.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donna's hand reaches for the ignition key and closes on it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Leaves the stalled car to name the trust we place in machines.
storyboard.addedInformation: The key is the object of that trust, shown as a deed.

explainedBy: When a machine fails, such as a flooded carburetor, we lose the human defenses we rely on.

storyboard.claim: A machine failure strips away our defenses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-step flow: machines fail, then defense is stripped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the key to the cause-and-effect of the failure.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the cause -> effect chain visible: failure, then loss of defense.

explainedBy: The failure drops us back down the food chain, as vulnerable as early humans.

storyboard.claim: The failure drops us down the food chain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same flow with a third step: food chain.
storyboard.onScreenText: Machines fail / Defense stripped / Food chain
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the third step to the same flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: The third step is the result: we are prey again.

explainedBy: The Pinto is now a metal cage baking in the sun.

storyboard.claim: The car is a metal cage baking in the sun.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sealed car box with heat waves rising from it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The flow ends; the car itself becomes the threat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The heat waves show the car as an oven.

explainedBy: Donna's ingrained driving habits are the one thing that saves them at first contact.

storyboard.claim: Donna's habits save them at the first moment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donna at the wheel, calm and focused.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the failure to the one thing that works.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the habit as the saving factor.

explainedBy: Her father drilled a specific parking routine into her head.

storyboard.claim: Her father taught her a parking routine.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donna, calm, at the wheel.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains where the habit came from.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the origin of the habit.

explainedBy: The last step of the routine is taking the keys out, done by reflex.

storyboard.claim: Donna takes the keys out as part of the routine.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donna's hand reaches for the ignition key and closes on it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same key as before, now taken out as a habit.
storyboard.addedInformation: The deed shows the routine as a physical action.

explainedBy: The automatic habit is the only thing that saves her throat from Kujo.

storyboard.claim: The habit saves her from Kujo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donna holding the key, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same key held; the saving is named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the habit to the threat.

explainedBy: Kujo lunges out of the dark at the moment she rolls the window up.

storyboard.claim: Kujo lunges out of the dark at the car.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donna afraid in the forest set, Kujo angry, close.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The threat enters, the car is no longer the only subject.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the dog and the woman in one frame.

explainedBy: The reflex taught decades ago is what keeps them alive.

storyboard.claim: The driver's ed reflex keeps them alive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same frame: Donna afraid, Kujo angry in the dark.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same frame; the reflex is named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the habit that saved them.

explainedBy: The hosts turn to criticizing Donna's decisions.

storyboard.claim: The hosts will criticize Donna.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donna worried, facing the criticism.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from her reflex to judging her decision.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the judgment being made.

explainedBy: The drive leads five miles out of town onto a dead-end road.

storyboard.claim: The drive ends on a dead-end road five miles out.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A road icon: a dead-end farm road.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the reflex to the place she drove to.
storyboard.addedInformation: The road is the dead end: no way in or out.

explainedBy: She could have left Tad safely at home with the sitter.

storyboard.claim: Donna could have left Tad at home.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A house icon: the home she could have stayed in.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the road to the home she left.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the alternative she did not take.

explainedBy: Judging her from the cold rationality of hindsight is the unfair part.

storyboard.claim: We judge her with hindsight.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donna worried, the judgment hanging over her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the alternative to the fairness of judging.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the stance of the hosts.

explainedBy: Kemp, her violent ex-lover, ambushed her in the kitchen and drove her out of her home.

storyboard.claim: Kemp ambushed Donna in her kitchen.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kemp angry in the kitchen, Donna afraid across from him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the reason she fled home.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the threat at home before the flight.

explainedBy: The house no longer felt safe: polluted, violated, dangerous.

storyboard.claim: Home has become dangerous.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A house icon with Donna afraid beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the kitchen to the house as a whole.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names how the house felt to her.

explainedBy: The broken car heading toward a rural mechanic felt like the lesser of two evils.

storyboard.claim: The car trip looked like the lesser evil.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sealed car box with Donna worried beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the house to the car she chose.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names her choice as a comparison.

explainedBy: Fleeing the human monster drives her right into a biological one.

storyboard.claim: She escapes a human monster and runs into a biological one.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-step flow: human monster, then biological monster.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the choice to the chain of threats.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cause -> effect of her flight.

explainedBy: The trauma of the domestic threat pushes her into the natural one: the broken machine over the broken man.

storyboard.claim: The domestic threat pushes her into the natural one.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same flow, unchanged.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same flow; the hosts restate it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Restates the chain without a new step.

explainedBy: Ordinary machines build the trap that holds them inside the car.

storyboard.claim: The trap is built from ordinary things.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sealed car box with Donna worried and Tad sad inside.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the flight to the car as a trap.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the car as the trap.

explainedBy: The hosts say this scene is painful to watch.

storyboard.claim: The scene is agony to watch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same car, both faces sad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same car; commentary on its pain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reaction only, no new information.

explainedBy: The phone rings inside the empty Camber house while they wait in the car.

storyboard.claim: The phone rings in the empty house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dead telephone with a red line through it; Donna worried and Tad sad in the car.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the car to the phone that cannot reach them.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dead-line phone shows the unreachable call.

explainedBy: They can hear the ringing through the walls, just out of reach.

storyboard.claim: The ringing comes through the walls.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same dead phone; Donna and Tad listening in the car.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same phone; the sound is named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the distance: heard but not reached.

explainedBy: The ringing drives Kujo into a bellowing frenzy at the car door.

storyboard.claim: The ringing sends Kujo into a frenzy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kujo angry at the car, Donna afraid inside.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the ringing to the dog's reaction.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the dog reacting to the sound.

explainedBy: The rabies virus makes the ringing hurt his brain, so he associates the pain with the humans in the car.

storyboard.claim: The ringing hurts the infected brain and the dog attacks the humans.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A causal chain: the ringing, then the infected brain, then the attack.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the frenzy to the mechanism behind it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the chain the narration explains.

explainedBy: The ringing acts like ice picks in the infected brain, so the dog turns on the humans in the car.

storyboard.claim: The ringing hurts the infected brain; the dog attacks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same causal chain; the ice token travels from the brain to the attack.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same chain, the next steps drawn.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the brain and the attack as the result.

explainedBy: The phone is just yards away, totally out of reach, and makes the dog more aggressive.

storyboard.claim: The phone is yards away and out of reach.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dead telephone with a red line through it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the dog's mechanism back to the phone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the distance that keeps the phone useless.

explainedBy: We believe help is only nine numbers away, but the line is dead.

storyboard.claim: Help is nine numbers away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same dead telephone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same phone; the belief in help is named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the belief that the phone is the rescue.

explainedBy: When the phone rings empty, the silence on the line isolates them more than no phone would.

storyboard.claim: The silence on a ringing phone is a weapon.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same dead telephone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same phone; the claim turns to the silence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the effect of the empty ring.

explainedBy: The phone becomes a torture device reminding Donna she is cut off from civilization.

storyboard.claim: The phone is a psychological torture device.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same dead telephone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same phone; the torture is named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the phone's effect on Donna.

explainedBy: Vic sits in a dark hotel room, dialing his home number endlessly.

storyboard.claim: Vic keeps dialing home.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Vic seated in a dark hotel room beside the dead telephone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the dead phone in the car to Vic's phone far away.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the same torture on Vic's end.

explainedBy: He lets the line ring twenty times, just waiting, instead of thinking clearly.

storyboard.claim: Vic lets the phone ring again and again.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Vic seated, the same dead telephone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the waiting is named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the waiting in the ring count.

explainedBy: The empty ringing feeds his deep-seated insecurities.

storyboard.claim: The empty ringing feeds Vic's insecurity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Vic seated, the same dead telephone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; what the ringing does to him.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the effect on Vic.

explainedBy: Because of the affair, Vic convinces himself Donna ran off with Kemp, and each ring confirms his fear.

storyboard.claim: Vic believes Donna ran off with Kemp.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Vic seated, worried, the same dead telephone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the belief is named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the fear each ring reinforces.
